terms.comment: Our description for a magnetic toy tile: Traupman and Morgan–Owens have no word for it. Tessella, tessellae f. is classically a little cube or square of stone for a pavement (Sen., Juv., in Lewis & Short); magnēticus is in Traupman (pp. 261, 343) and Morgan–Owens (after Egger).

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 261, 343.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. magnetic.
